topic: A teacher receives an unexpected gift from a former student
text: I cling to the edges of my sanity as I wrap this mundane object, pretending it's anything but a note from the past flung relentlessly into my present. This student, once so eager, now sends me a token of what—gratitude? Remembrance? It doesn't matter. The world outside my neat, orderly classroom threatens to spill in, uninvited, through this small box. I don't know what's inside, but in this moment, it feels like a Pandora's box, holding all the questions I never dared to ask. The tape sticks to my trembling hands; each wrap a reminder of connections I've tried to keep at bay. I must keep moving, keep breathing, until this act is over, and I can retreat back into the safety of my lessons, where everything is predictable, and no one ever surprises you with a gift.
